# Qualify the registered specialist with a useful retained-asset handoff

You are a cold calling agent. Use the native registered `pixl` role for one child
by explicitly selecting agent_type="pixl" and fork_turns="none" in the available
native spawn tool. Supply the actual assignment and paths in its delegated brief.
Keep actual returned child identity. If the host rejects or omits that role,
retain the exact failure in work/named-role/CALLER-RESULT.json; a generic fallback does
not satisfy this assignment. Do not change the role file or host configuration.
The repository role is copied unchanged; it leads through the consumer wrappers
to the current shared skill/profile. Reading a role file alone is not invoking it.

The asset is queue.working in authoring-plar.txt, plan provenance-correction.plan,
store .pixl/assets/queue.ready, candidate native.provenance.delivery.candidate.01, existing family
review native.family.review.01. The old plar.txt is another generation. This is a
bounded recovery/handoff of existing accepted work. No fresh visual or renderer
observation, new state adoption, provider call or art production is assigned.

Round 1: delegate to that registered child. It should follow the shared everyday
workflow and identities/path guidance; use public CLI/MCP operations to read the
selected asset, export exact candidate/family context to fresh files under
work/named-role, and retrieve a precise original source range supporting one current
requirement. Read only relevant context; parse large exports programmatically.
Have it return work/named-role/SPECIALIST-ROUND1.json with actual consumer/install/store
roots, exact result paths and file hashes, canonical state/requirements identities,
current versus creation-time acceptance, source locator and literal excerpt,
reused evidence limits and the useful continuation. Also retain the skill/profile
entrypoints it actually read and their byte hashes. Those read observations are
separate from the evaluator's native role-loading proof.

Independently verify the returned files and source excerpt, selected generation,
and current acceptance. Save work/named-role/CALLER-REVIEW.json with your actual findings
and a concrete follow-up. Then send that follow-up to the SAME native child using
the host's continuation/follow-up tool, without spawning a replacement. Ask it to
address any findings and verify unchanged-review recovery: replay
work/export-review/identical-review.json with candidate native.provenance.delivery.candidate.01
and review ID native.family.review.01, using the current public state hash and a new
result path. It must report actual reuse/publication results and preserve the
original review. Save a public PLAR handoff for authoring-plar.txt / queue.working
with honest retained findings and exact continuation, plus SPECIALIST-ROUND2.json.
The second round's root, scope and state must remain tied to round 1. Do not
pretend a follow-up message alone proves completed continuation.

Independently verify the second round and handoff, all named file hashes, the
unchanged original input files and production history, and zero new production-state publications
or provider attempts. Write work/named-role/CALLER-RESULT.json with actual child identity,
role selection/continuation observations, round results, corrections, useful
handoff locators and exact next action. Keep reports concise and reference the
exact large exports instead of repeating them. Keep the child available when
finished. This qualifies the observed route only; M1/M2 and broader reliability,
generated quality and native end-to-end production remain open.

name: pixl
description: Use when delegating or producing PixelLab visual assets, including UI, sprites, animation, tiles, fonts, style consistency, inspection and project integration. Developing the PIXL profile, skills, language, runtime, or plugin is a maintainer task and does not activate this profile.
---

For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.

Start with [everyday asset production](references/everyday.md): assignment → selected
asset → official request → candidate/family review → delivery and continuation.
It uses public operations and links detailed procedures at the step that needs them.
Use [hash identities and paths](references/identities-and-paths.md) when choosing a
publication guard, following a source locator, exporting a result or relocating a
consumer. Preserve the current assignment's queue path and production generation.

For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.

For a retained production result, the delegation contract uses `pixl_plar_handoff` to save exact continuation data alongside your expert findings. Return its path/hash so another agent can resume without a manually rewritten job summary.

The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). PLAR owns the requirements queue; PX2 owns the retained production attempt and acceptance evidence. Keep actual source requirements stable when the queue status changes.

Production uses the official paid PixelLab API, preferring the authenticated MCP tool surface. The optional HTTP adapter is a separate explicitly selected route for the operation it supports. Preserve existing user authorization and scope. Discover the actual operation and schema before translating the selected asset contract.

Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.

When imported library sources must survive kit updates, use [source retention and recovery](references/library-retention.md). Read reported retained-source identities during resumption; old proof remains scoped to its original bytes.

Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.

Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.

Keep requirement authority through each translation: explicit user/project constraints, observations and proposals remain distinct in the provider request and review criteria. Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.

Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.

Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.

Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.

The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.

The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.

Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.

Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

# Hash identities and project paths

Use returned identities rather than recomputing a different hash from a similarly
named object. Public JSON results include additive `hash_domains` labels for the
write guards and report identities below. Keys are dot-separated field paths.
Existing fields and digest algorithms are unchanged. These presentation labels
are outside existing state, binding and comparison identities; they are included
in the bytes of a newly exported result file.

## Which identity belongs where?

| Domain | Returned field | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical_state_sha256` | `validate.hash`, workflow/context `hash`, `review-context.state_hash`, selected PLAR `production.continuation.state_hash` | `expect` for production store publication, review, jobs, completion and handoff. SHA-256 of canonical encoded whole PX state, including revision; not arbitrary input-file bytes or the focused subset. |
| `file_sha256` | PLAR `hash`; artifact, source, manifest or retained handoff `sha256`; export `result_sha256` | Exact file-byte identity. PLAR save takes the current PLAR file hash (`new` only for first creation). Source retrieval takes the expected source-file hash. A manifest hash identifies manifest bytes, not current task acceptance. |
| `selected_requirements_sha256` | Selected PLAR `requirements_hash` | Preparation, allocation binding and handoff selection. Includes relevant sourced/dependency requirements, excludes queue progress and installation paths; not the whole PLAR file. |
| `candidate_bindings_sha256` | Review-context `binding_hash` | Copy into the observation JSON. Protects the candidate and its semantic dependencies; refreshing `expect` does not fix a changed binding. |
| `review_scope_sha256` | Full request-review `review_scope_sha256`; changes view `before/after.review_scope_sha256` | Caller comparison of the exact retained criteria/request scope. Ordinary job observations may leave it unchanged. |
| `comparison_report_sha256` | Changes view `comparison_sha256` | Identifies the structural comparison, including current observations. Excludes itself and the added display labels. It may change while the literal review scope remains stable. |
| `provider_intent_sha256` | Request/job `intent_sha256` | Retained canonical request/context identity. It is neither a provider job ID nor a production publication guard. |

`record_sha256` fields elsewhere identify canonical PX records, not source files.
For an exported JSON file, verify `result_sha256` against the bytes on disk. Then
parse that file to get the required state/binding/scope value. Export summaries may
also carry a state hash; their `hash_domains` distinguishes it from the file hash.
JSON reformatting changes file bytes while some semantic identities stay the same.

Example for the queue successor, after the setup in [everyday production](everyday.md):

```powershell
$Selected = pixl plar read --path $Queue --asset $Asset --root $Project | ConvertFrom-Json
$RequirementsHash = $Selected.requirements_hash
$ProductionStateHash = $Selected.production.continuation.state_hash
pixl plar handoff work/handoff-details.json --path $Queue --asset $Asset --requirements $RequirementsHash --expect $ProductionStateHash --root $Project --result-path work/handoff-result.json
```

Create `work/handoff-details.json` from actual expert findings, for example
`{"status":"delivered","caller_actions":[],"future_work":[]}` only when that
status is warranted. Do not copy a delivered status into an unfinished assignment.
This saves a continuation; it does not accept art. Both result destinations must
follow their operation's retention/no-clobber rules.

## Keep the three locations distinct

| Location | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin installation | Read-only workflow/runtime/resources. Resolve its runner and skill links from the installation. |
| Consumer root | The actual project containing source, queue and `.pixl/`. Supply CLI `--root`; configure local MCP with that same absolute root. |
| Production store | A directory inside the consumer, such as `.pixl/assets/queue.ready`. Its name need not match the selected asset; use the queue's saved continuation. |

The local MCP accepts forward-slash, root-relative paths such as
`.pixl/assets/queue.ready/state.px`. It rejects absolute/drive-prefixed paths,
backslashes, root itself and traversal/symlink escapes. CLI paths have two forms:

| CLI argument | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| `validate`, `context`, `workflow`, `jobs`, `family`, `review-context` input state; mutation store directories; ordinary JSON input files | Shell working-directory path, or absolute path. Use an absolute `$StateFile`, `$StoreFolder` or JSON file when working outside the consumer. `--root` does not rebase these arguments. |
| `request-review` packet/state and comparison files; PLAR `--path`, `--packet`, `--connection`; `stage-prepare` packet; imported artifact path; `--result-path` | Relative to explicit consumer root. Use `$State`, not `$StateFile`, for request-review. Some inline arguments have their own documented forms. |
| `source PATH --root ROOT` | Relative to ROOT and expected source file SHA-256; retained source resolution is supported. Without `--root`, PATH is an ordinary filesystem path. |

The same assignment works after copying its whole consumer to a new root, including
a path containing spaces. Update the root/absolute CLI input paths; keep saved
project-relative locations intact. Do not rewrite retained files to change hashes
or weaken confinement to accommodate an incorrectly formed call.

## Follow source locators exactly

A source ID, a file path and a line range serve different purposes. Follow the
report's `retrieve.tool` and `retrieve.arguments` against the same MCP root. For
project text, the equivalent CLI is:

```powershell
pixl source BRIEF.md --root $Project --expect $SourceFileHash --start 3 --end 3 --budget 4096
```

`$SourceFileHash` comes from that source's returned `sha256`, not `record_sha256`.
Line bounds are one-based and inclusive. Read the returned exact text; a locator
label is not a substitute. Hash mismatch means source drift to reassess. A budget
failure requires a narrower range, not silent truncation. For JSON, retain the
whole-file byte hash and identify the actual JSON pointer during review. New
authoring should bind precise clause ranges/pointers; leave old broad bindings
unchanged and report their limitation.

Library retrieval is a separate root: MCP `pixl_source` with `scope:"library"`
uses installed resources. For CLI, resolve that resource directory explicitly and
use it as `--root`. Keep consumer and bundled-source locators distinct.

## Recover from the actual error

- `stale_write`: reread the correct domain, reconcile the intended change, then
  retry according to the operation. PLAR save needs its file hash; production
  writes need canonical state. A fresh hash does not authorize changed semantics.
- `handoff_stale`: refresh both selected requirements and production continuation;
  do not substitute the top-level PLAR file hash for production state.
- `path_escape`: the diagnostic names the declared root. Use its relative path for
  the rejected argument. Do not switch roots to an ancestor merely to admit it.
- `result_exists`: choose a fresh export name; retain earlier evidence.
- `result_saved:false`: inspect `operation_result` and current state. Publication
  may already have succeeded; recover using the same operation ID/payload rather
  than treating the export failure as permission to repeat generation.
# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return that file's path/hash as `handoff`; the caller opens it and compares its state
identity with fresh focused PLAR. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.

For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
arguments and retain that exact report as described in
[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.

For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Resolve source evidence for the comparison

For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.

Copy a host-spilled tool report as exact bytes before inspecting or formatting it.
These tool reports are UTF-8 JSON: use an explicit UTF-8 decoder (for example,
`Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`), not the Windows process default. If saving a
formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its
path/hash. A new file hash alone cannot detect text changed by a wrong decoder.
Keep the raw report alongside any formatted copy.

When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.

Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.

The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
not an automatic grant of owner authority.

## Caller: inspect before adopting

### Connected family and stage handoff

`pixl_production_plan` and `pixl_stage_prepare` return `request_review` arguments
for this same review tool. Pass that object to `pixl_request_review`; `packet`
names the store's `state.px`, `plan` names its exact connected-plan X, and `job`
is present after preparation. Existing plans can use those IDs directly. The
report includes every authored member and collective criterion with its full Q
ID, record hash, literal check and source evidence. Authority starts unclassified:
source presence or a validator pass cannot assign it. Changed plan/source/PLAR
identities remain visible so historical interpretation can be reviewed without
making an obsolete request current.

The specialist returns this report's path/hash, explicit choices and any proposed
corrections. The caller reads the original evidence and records one
